title: Stadtturm Rattenberg (Augustiner-Museum)
name: Stadtturm Rattenberg (Augustiner-Museum)
kurzbeschreibung: The historic church and town tower in Rattenberg: baroque belfry, Augustinian-Servite museum with sacred art treasures, and panoramic views of the Inn.
beschreibung:
Overview

The imposing Stadtturm Rattenberg (which also serves as the prominent steeple of the former Augustinian Hermits monastery church) towers above the historic glassmaking town of Rattenberg in the Tyrolean Unterinntal. With fewer than 500 inhabitants, Rattenberg is renowned as Austria's smallest town, boasting an almost completely preserved medieval townscape. Together with the Augustiner-Museum Rattenberg, the fortified late-Gothic tower forms the cultural heart of the town, offering visitors a captivating journey into the sacred art of the Tyrolean Unterland and the storied history of navigation along the Inn River.

History & Augustinian Museum

The Augustinian Hermits monastery was founded in 1385 by Duke Johann of Bavaria to bolster the spiritual and cultural importance of the Bavarian border fortress of Rattenberg; in 1504, under Emperor Maximilian I, the town became permanently part of Tyrol. In the early 20th century, the Servite Order took over the monastery. The distinctive church tower was built in the late Middle Ages and received its baroque redesign in the 18th century. Since 1993, the entire monastic complex has housed the award-winning Augustiner-Museum Rattenberg: it exhibits masterworks of Gothic sculpture, late-baroque altarpieces, precious goldsmith art from Tyrolean workshops, and ornate liturgical vestments. An architectural highlight of any visit is the ascent via a secured wooden staircase up into the historic belfry: passing massive bronze bells, visitors emerge onto the airy watchman's platform, which affords a breathtaking 360-degree panorama over the colourful Gothic rooftops of the old town, the navigable Inn River, the castle ruins on the Schlossberg, and the craggy flanks of the Rofangebirge.

Visit & Getting There

The Augustiner-Museum and the Stadtturm are open seasonally from early May to late October from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed on Mondays). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youths under 18 years enjoy free admission. Holders of the regional Alpbachtal Card receive free admission. Getting there by public transport: by regional ÖBB train (S-Bahn Tirol) to Bahnhof Rattenberg-Kramsach; from there, it is just an easy three-minute flat walk through the town gate directly to the museum. By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Kramsach/Brixlegg; as Rattenberg is a completely car-free pedestrian zone, paid parking spaces (P1 to P3) are available immediately outside the town gates.

Tips

The climb up into the belfry chamber is via historic timber steps and is not wheelchair-accessible (surefootedness required); the Gothic cloister and the ground-floor exhibition rooms offer low-threshold, level access. Combine your tower visit with a glassblowing demonstration in one of the town's traditional Glasbläsereien workshops and take a scenic walk up to the castle ruins on the Schlossberg.
